Explain the informal argument for the area of a circle.
items.answer: Slicing the circle into many thin wedges and alternating them forms a shape close to a rectangle whose height is the radius $r$ and whose width is half the circumference $\pi r$, so the area is $\pi r\cdot r=\pi r^2$.

steps: Rearranged wedges approximate a rectangle of area $\pi r^2$.
